speaker: Doctor
text: I will begin by asking: How long have you had this painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg, and can you describe exactly what it looks like and where on the leg it is located?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum. The clinical picture of a rapidly progressing, painful ulcer on the leg in a patient with a history of Crohn's disease and diabetes is highly suggestive of Pyoderma Gangrenosum, likely triggered by the recalled insect bite. The history of anterior uveitis and steroid use further supports an underlying inflammatory or autoimmune predisposition.
